reports.content:
# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — Runner autodetect + trusted central model catalogue

Task: `9d2b75a2-1ecd-47ce-a9f9-b3068c5f5cf7`
Author: planning turn (no code changed yet)
Inputs: task brief, `SURVEY.md` (this folder; questions present, `answers: {}`
empty), codebase evidence below. The brief also names
`idea-20261111-074628.md`, which does not exist in this folder — treated as
missing input, not as evidence.

## Goal

Runners reliably autodetect the models their harnesses can serve (muse first,
then every other leg that shares the bug); those ids are normalized to the
KainBain canonical key grammar, saved into one central model catalogue; and
the UI selects exclusively from that central list — including brand-new
models (e.g. the latest Muse release) and fleet-only harnesses — without
ever silently wiping alias targets.

## Success criteria

1. A new model released in a harness appears as a selectable UI option through
   the normal detection path (no hand-editing of pins or allowlists).
2. One documented central catalogue is the single source the pickers read;
   each option carries its harness attribution and availability.
3. Changing harness availability (offline runner, empty scan, malformed id)
   degrades honestly (marked unavailable / explained warning), never silently.
4. Alias targets are never silently wiped or retargeted by detection changes;
   a missing saved choice keeps the last working value with a warning.
5. `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` pass; new behaviour is pinned by
   committed tests.

## Current architecture (verified evidence)

- Runner detection: `runner/daemon.js` (`detectAvailableHarnesses`,
  `refreshDiscoveredModels`, `factsFor`, `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS`),
  per-harness legs in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` reusing each
  backend harness's `listModels()`; muse leg probes `muse serve` stdio
  `model/list` (`runner/modelDiscovery.js` `discoverClaudeModels`).
  Advertisement is pin-wins by default (`resolveAdvertisedModels`),
  discovery-wins opt-in (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`),
  12 h cadence (`MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS_DEFAULT`), keep-old-slice on
  failure; heartbeat carries `facts.models` + `facts.discoveryStatus`.
- Backend serves TWO catalogues: engine catalogue
  (`aggregateModelCatalog` in `api/models.js`, local harnesses only,
  TTL-cached, curated `FALLBACK_MODELS`) at `GET /compute/models`; fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog` in
  `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.js`, live-derived from runner
  registrations, never persisted) at `GET /runners/models/catalogue`
  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`).
- Frontend: `useModelCatalog` reads `/compute/models` (single fetch point);
  `useFleetModelCatalog` reads fleet counts; `ModelSelector` merges fleet
  ids into backend harness sections via `withFleetModels` /
  `fleetModelsForHarness` (`frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/`).
  Sections come from the backend `harnesses[]` view — there is no section
  for a harness the backend host itself does not know.
- Grammar: canonical `harness::provider::id(::reasoning)` in
  `shared/modelKeys.js` (single implementation shared backend/frontend).
  The brief's `harness::model::effort` is read as: canonical key + effort
  (tiers/reasoning) carried as catalogue attributes — see Open questions.
- Aliases: `shared/modelAliases.js`; `normalizeModelAliases` drops invalid
  records on write; `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` clears the model on harness
  change (`onTargetChange({ harness: next, model: '' })`); unknown-model is
  currently soft (badge + save succeeds); ADR 0005 owns dispatch combination
  rules.

## Survey mapping (SURVEY.md answers are empty — defaults proposed)

| # | Question | Proposed default (reversible) |
|---|----------|-------------------------------|
| q1 | Scope: muse-only vs all harnesses | Muse first, others only if the same bug affects them |
| q2 | New-model latency | Automatic on next detection/heartbeat; manual Refresh stays as escape hatch |
| q3 | Central list shape | One combined list, each entry labelled with source harness |
| q4 | Offline/broken/empty ids | Keep showing, marked unavailable, with reason |
| q5 | Saved alias choice goes missing | Keep last working choice + warning (never silent wipe) |
| q6 | New model moves aliases? | No — aliases stay; new model is an extra option |

These defaults are assumed unless the task owner answers the survey; each is
flagged at its implementation step so an answer can flip it cheaply.

## Approach — make change easy, then make the change

Research and the two structural enablers come first (Phases 0–1): prove the
exact break in each symptom chain with a failing test before touching
behaviour, and build the seams (fixtures, contract tests, provenance logging)
that make the later fix small and reviewable. Behaviour changes land after
(Phases 2–5), one symptom per phase, each independently shippable.

## Steps

### Phase 0 — Diagnose with evidence (research first, no behaviour change)

0.1. Trace the new-Muse-model chain end to end and record where the id drops:
runner leg output → `facts.models` → fleet catalogue (`harnesses` union +
section gate) → `/compute/models` sections → `withFleetModels` merge.
Prime suspects to confirm or rule out, in order: (a) no backend `muse`
harness section exists so fleet-only muse ids have nowhere to render;
(b) the `serving` gate in `fleetModelsForHarness` excludes the id because
the runner's advertised `harnesses` union lacks `muse`; (c) the runner leg
drops the row (`modelDiscovery.js` skips any provider/model containing
`:` while `modelKeys.js` allows single `:` in ids); (d) pin-wins +
12 h cadence hides the discovery result; (e) TTL caches
(`modelListCache`, MSP catalogue 5 min, client 60 s) delay visibility.
0.2. Reproduce the alias wipe: harness-change clear in
`ModelAliasesSection.jsx`, `normalizeModelAliases` drops on save/load, and
any picker path that rewrites a stored unknown-model value. Record which
path(s) fire for the muse-alias report.
0.3. Audit every other discovery leg (`pi`, `antigravity`, `vibe`,
`opencode`, `codex`) for the same defect class found in 0.1 (q1 scope
decision is evidence-led: shared bug ⇒ shared fix).
0.4. Write findings to `ROOT_CAUSE.md` in this task folder (chain diagram +
per-suspect CONFIRMED/RULED-OUT with file:line + log/test excerpt).

### Phase 1 — Make change easy (seams, fixtures, contracts; no behaviour change)

1.1. Add a mock-`muse serve` transcript fixture containing the new-model row
(extend `api/agent/harnesses/muse/fixtures/`) plus a mock runner
registration fixture, so the whole chain is testable without the real CLI.
1.2. Add contract tests pinning the catalogue seam: runner-discovered id ⇒
fleet catalogue entry `{ id, harnesses, tiers, runnerCount }` ⇒ UI option
with identical key (dispatch matches verbatim, so keys must be byte-equal).
1.3. Add provenance logging: each catalogue entry traces to
(runner id, harness leg, detected-at); surface `discoveryStatus` per
harness in the existing Settings › Runners surface (already partially
there — fill gaps only).
1.4. Reconcile the `harness::model::effort` naming: document the canonical
grammar + where effort/tiers live (catalogue attributes, see Open
questions) in `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md`.

### Phase 2 — Fix runner autodetect (muse first, shared bugs everywhere)

2.1. Fix the confirmed muse-leg drop (whichever of 0.1a–e it is). If the
colon filter is at fault, align the leg with `parseModelKey` instead of
its own stricter rule.
2.2. Apply the identical fix to every leg sharing the defect (0.3); legs
with honestly-empty semantics (`codex`, unconfigured `opencode`) keep
their classified errors, only the shared defect class is fixed.
2.3. If pin-wins/cadence is (partly) hiding discovery: keep pin-wins as the
default (upgrade-safe) but make the effective source visible per runner
(pinned vs discovered, last scan time) and ensure Re-detect scans and
reports honestly. Do not flip the default without a survey answer.
2.4. Gate: new-model fixture row flows runner → fleet catalogue in tests.

### Phase 3 — One trusted central catalogue (the structural change)

3.1. Decide persisted snapshot vs live-derived (recommendation: keep the
live derivation as the computation, add a persisted snapshot with
provenance + detected-at so the UI never depends on a transient read;
mark entries stale/unavailable rather than deleting them — survey q4).
Record the decision in an ADR.
3.2. Normalize every runner-advertised id through `parseModelKey` /
`normalizeModelRef` at ingestion; malformed ids are quarantined with a
reason (visible in Settings), never silently dropped, never served.
3.3. Ensure fleet-only harnesses get catalogue sections: the central list's
harness set is the UNION of backend-known and fleet-served harnesses
(fixes 0.1a class permanently for every future harness).
3.4. Gate: central-list endpoint returns the new-model entry with harness
label + availability after a single runner heartbeat in tests.

### Phase 4 — UI selects from the central list only

4.1. Repoint all pickers (`ModelSelector`, project default, stage override,
alias targets) at the central list; backend-only and fleet-only entries
render uniformly with harness labels (survey q3) and availability badges.
4.2. Unavailable entries (offline runner, stale snapshot, quarantined id)
render marked-unavailable with reasons (survey q4), never hidden, never
normal-looking.
4.3. Keep Refresh (backend `?refresh=true` + Re-detect) as the manual escape
hatch; automatic appearance on next detection remains the default path
(survey q2).
4.4. Visual check via `npm run capture:screenshot` or existing headless
fixtures only — no long-lived dev servers.

### Phase 5 — Alias trust (no wipe, no silent retarget)

5.1. Stop the wipe: harness change preserves the model text (badge
unknown-model instead of clearing); persistence never drops a target the
user saved — invalid records quarantine with a warning, matching the
q5 keep-last-working default.
5.2. New models never move aliases (q6 default): aliases resolve to stored
targets only; the new model appears as an extra pickable option.
5.3. Gate: regression tests — save muse alias target, simulate catalogue
churn (model disappears / harness offline / new model arrives), assert
the stored target byte-survives with a warning surfaced.

### Phase 6 — Assurance and rollout

6.1. Full gates: `npm run test:unit`, `npm run lint`, plus any configured
analyser gate found in the repo (check package.json/CI before finishing).
6.2. Update docs: `HarnessModelSelector.md` (central list as the seam),
`ModelKeys.md` (grammar + effort), `runner/README.md` (legs matrix +
effective-source visibility), Settings help text.
6.3. Rollout is additive: old runners (no provenance) read as unknown-source
entries; rollback per phase (Phase 4 can revert to the merged view without
losing Phase 2 detection fixes).

## Validation plan (per phase, evidence-oriented)

- 0.x: `ROOT_CAUSE.md` with CONFIRMED/RULED-OUT per suspect + a failing test
  per confirmed break (red before, green after — the test is written from
  the observed real behaviour, not from the fix assumption).
- 1.x: contract tests pass; no behavioural test changes needed (pure
  refactoring/fixtures ⇒ existing suite stays green).
- 2.x–5.x: each phase's Gate test + the full `npm run test:unit` suite;
  edge/error paths exercised per phase (empty scan, malformed id, offline
  runner, unknown-harness fleet id, blank alias model on `none` harness).
- Highest-risk check: Phase 3→4 integration — a fleet-only harness id must
  be selectable AND dispatchable (key byte-equality from picker to
  `effectiveRunnerModels` match); verify with the dispatch-level test, not
  just the UI render.

## Testing plan

- Primary gate: unit/integration suites (`npm run test:unit`); no separate
  manual QA cycle required for logic changes.
- New committed tests colocated with touched areas (runner legs,
  `fleetModelCatalog`, `modelKeys` ingestion, `ModelSelector` /
  `ModelAliasesSection`, dispatch matching).
- Throwaway probes (if needed) live under `/tmp`, never committed.
- UI changes verified headless (`npm run capture:screenshot`, existing
  fixtures/mocks); no background servers.

## Documentation plan

- `ROOT_CAUSE.md` (this folder): diagnosis evidence from Phase 0.
- ADR (this repo's `docs/adr/`): persisted-snapshot vs live-derived
  decision + catalogue ownership.
- Updates: `docs/EngineDetails/HarnessModelSelector.md`,
  `docs/EngineDetails/ModelKeys.md`, `runner/README.md`, Settings copy.
- CHANGELOG entry if the repo convention calls for one.

## Risks / open questions

1. SURVEY.md has no answers — all six survey decisions ride on the proposed
   defaults above; a late answer flips implementation cheaply only before
   its phase lands. Highest leverage: q4 (hide vs mark unavailable) and q6
   (alias auto-switch).
2. `harness::model::effort` vs canonical `harness::provider::id(::reasoning)`:
   assumed the brief means canonical key + effort as attributes (tiers in
   the fleet catalogue, reasoning segment in keys). If the task owner means
   a NEW 3-part `harness::model::effort` key format, Phase 1.4 must design
   a migration instead — confirm before Phase 3.
3. Persisted snapshot adds a staleness problem the live view avoids; the
   mitigation is provenance + staleness marking (never silent delete).
   If persistence proves unnecessary during Phase 3, the fallback is:
   live-derived central computation + fixed UI sourcing, no new store.
4. MRS / multi-runner conflicts (same id, different tiers): union today;
   keep unioning unless Phase 0 shows dispatch mismatches from it.

## Non-goals

- New harnesses, new providers, or new model families beyond detection reach.
- Changing dispatch matching semantics (verbatim id match stays).
- Stored-format migrations of existing `defaultModel`/alias values (ADR 0005
  additive-seam constraint stands).
- Flipping pin-wins to discovery-wins globally.

reports.name: ROOT_CAUSE.md
reports.content:
# ROOT_CAUSE — Runner autodetect + model catalogue (task 9d2b75a2)

Phase 0 diagnosis. Chain under test:

```
muse CLI model/list → runner leg → facts.models → heartbeat →
fleet catalogue → /compute/models sections → withFleetModels merge → picker
```

A second chain covers aliases: stored target → load sanitize →
editor draft → save validation → persisted.

Verdicts use CONFIRMED (breaks the chain) / RULED-OUT / CONDITIONAL
(real mechanism, fires only in some configurations).

## Suspect verdicts (plan 0.1)

### (a) No backend `muse` harness section — RULED-OUT (as stated)

The backend always registers all 8 harnesses including `muse`
(`api/crew/harnessRoster.js:143-155`), so `/compute/models`
`harnesses[]` always carries a `muse` entry and `withFleetModels`
always has a section to merge fleet muse ids into.

BUT the entry can be `modelSelection: "none"` with `models: []`
(see suspect (f)): user-visible effect is near-identical ("nowhere to
select a muse model") whenever the fleet does not serve muse.

### (b) The `serving` gate — CONFIRMED mechanism, CONDITIONAL trigger

`fleetModelsForHarness` (`frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/fleetModelsForHarness.js:38`)
drops a harness-scoped id from its own section when the fleet entry's
serving-harness union is non-empty and lacks that harness. Fires
whenever a runner advertises muse ids without `muse` in its
configured harnesses (stale harness pin, manual model pin, harnessAuto
missing the CLI). Silent drop, no warning.

### (c) Runner muse-leg colon filter — CONFIRMED

`runner/modelDiscovery.js:132` drops any row whose provider or model
contains `:`:

```js
if (!provider || !model || provider.includes(":") || model.includes(":")) continue;
```

The shared grammar explicitly allows single `:` in ids
(`shared/modelKeys.js:16-18`, e.g. `glm-5.3-flash:cloud`), the
curated fallback is full of `:cloud` ids, and the backend MSP parser
(`parseMuseMspModels`) has no such filter — so backend-MSP and the
runner leg disagree: the backend would serve the id while the runner
silently drops it. Any new `muse serve` row with a `:` in
provider/model never reaches `facts.models`.

### (d) Pin-wins + 12 h cadence — CONFIRMED (by design, but invisible)

- Pinned runners skip scanning entirely (`runner/daemon.js:747`).
- Unpinned runners scan at boot + every 12 h
  (`MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS_DEFAULT`, `runner/modelDiscovery.js:187`).

A new model stays hidden until the next round (or forever when
pinned). The effective source (pinned vs discovered, last scan time)
is not visible per runner anywhere in the UI.

### (e) TTL caches — CONFIRMED as delay, not loss

`modelListCache` (backend, `config.modelCacheTtlMs`), MSP catalogue
5 min (`MUSE_MSP_MODEL_CACHE_TTL_MS`), client 60 s
(`MODELS_CACHE_TTL_MS`). `?refresh=true` / Refresh bypasses all
three. Delay-only; cannot permanently hide a model.

### (f) Transport-dependent muse `modelSelection` — CONFIRMED (primary break)

`api/agent/harnesses/muse/museHarness.js:562`:

```js
modelSelection: transport === "msp" ? "list" : "none",
```

`auto` engages MSP only when the resolved binary advertises `serve`
(`selectMuseTransport`, `museMspSupport.js:400`); otherwise the
backend runs exec and muse is `none`. Consequences:

1. `/compute/models` muse entry is `none` + `models: []`; the picker
   renders "This harness manages its own model" and offers NO model
   control unless the fleet serves muse (`effectiveModelSelection`
   none→list flip). New muse models are unselectable on exec
   backends with no fleet coverage.
2. Alias wipe on load (see W1 below).
3. Alias save refusal (see W2 below).

Note the exec transport DOES consume a model (`--model` plumbing,
`museHarness.js:693-696`), so `none` means "no catalogue to pick
from", not "model meaningless" — destroying stored muse models is
data loss, not cleanup.

### (g) Operator allowlist shadow — CONFIRMED mechanism, by design

`effectiveRunnerModels` (`api/flow/dispatch/runnerMatches/effectiveRunnerModels.js:14`)
replaces the advertised list with `operatorConfig.availableModels`
when set. A stale allowlist hides runner-discovered new models from
BOTH the fleet catalogue and dispatch. Consistent, but there is no
staleness signal.

## Alias wipe verdicts (plan 0.2)

### W1 Load-path blanking — CONFIRMED (the reported wipe)

`sanitizeAliasTargetModels` (`api/aliasTargets.js:458-483`) blanks
the model on every `none`-harness target at project load
(`api/projectStore.js:393-399`), and the next save persists the
blanked row. Whenever the backend muse transport is exec, EVERY
project load wipes EVERY muse alias target model. Console-only
warning; the stored value is destroyed.

### W2 Save-time hard refusal — CONFIRMED

`validateAliasTargetModels` (`api/aliasTargets.js:242-249`)
hard-refuses muse+model when `modelSelectionFor(muse)` is `none`.
The projects routes wire fleet-aware probes
(`api/routes/projects.js:43-47`, `api/index.js:254` + `:301`), so the
refusal lifts while the fleet serves muse — and returns the moment
fleet coverage lapses. Flapping gate.

### W3 UI harness-change clear — CONFIRMED (user-action-triggered)

`ModelAliasesSection.jsx:584` (and `:719` in the blocked-level
notice) clears the draft model on harness switch. Silent draft data
loss; saving persists it.

### W4 `normalizeModelAliases` drops — RULED-OUT as churn wipe

It drops only structurally invalid records (bad name, bad percent,
non-object) and never consults a catalogue, so catalogue churn
cannot invalidate a saved alias through this path.

### W5 Picker rewrite of unknown models — RULED-OUT

`modelKeyForValue` returns the stored value verbatim when
unresolvable, drafts (not resolved values) are saved, unknown-model
is soft (`targetValidity` → badge + save succeeds), and
`SelectDropdown` never fires `onChange` by itself. The stored value
survives catalogue churn in the UI.

## Other-leg audit (plan 0.3)

The colon-drop defect class is muse-runner-leg-only:

| Leg | Verdict |
|---|---|
| `pi` | OK — serves SDK ids verbatim; honest-empty `PI_MODELS_EMPTY` |
| `muse` (runner) | BROKEN — `:` filter (suspect c) |
| `muse` (backend MSP) | OK — no colon filter |
| `antigravity` | OK — `withModelKey`, single `:` fine; classified errors retained |
| `vibe` | OK — `withModelKey`, single `:` fine; retained errors |
| `opencode` | OK for `:`, note: `::`-bearing rows skipped silently in try/catch (`runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js:635-639`); string rows pass through to leg validation which drops invalid ids silently when siblings are valid (`runDiscoveryLeg`, `:213-231`) |
| `codex` | OK — honest-empty by design (`CODEX_DISCOVERY_UNAVAILABLE`) |

Latent (out of scope, noted): `withModelKey` THROWS on
`::`-containing ids, so one weird agy/vibe row fails the whole
parse into a classified error instead of quarantining the row.

## Failing tests (red → green)

Written in Phase 1.2, all red on this tree before the fix:

1. `runner/modelDiscovery.test.js`: `muse serve` row with single-`:` id
   flows through `discoverClaudeModels` (suspect c).
2. `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog` quarantine test: malformed
   runner-advertised id is quarantined with a reason, never served
   (plan 3.2; no quarantine exists today).
3. Route test: `/compute/models` carries a union section for a
   fleet-only harness id after one runner heartbeat (plan 3.3).
4. `api/aliasTargets.test.js` + project load test: muse alias target
   model survives load+save on an exec backend with a warning (W1).
5. `ModelAliasesSection` test: harness switch preserves the draft
   model (W3).

## Chain diagram (muse new-model, exec backend + healthy runner)

```
muse CLI model/list (new row, e.g. id with ':')
  │  backend exec: no backend listing at all (listModels → [])
  ▼
runner leg probes `muse serve` stdio
  │  ✗ (c) ':' row dropped   ✗ (d) pinned/12h hides scan
  ▼
facts.models ──heartbeat──▶ registry capabilities
  │  ✗ (g) operator allowlist replaces list
  ▼
fleet catalogue (live-derived, never persisted)
  │  ✗ offline/paused runner: entry vanishes silently
  ▼
/compute/models muse section (none + []) + fleet merge
  │  ✗ (b) serving gate drops id when runner harnesses lack muse
  │  ✗ (e) TTLs delay visibility
  ▼
picker: "manages its own model" OR option without the new id
```

And the alias chain on an exec backend:

```
stored {harness:'muse', model:'muse::meta::x'}
  │  ✗ (W1) load sanitize blanks model → next save persists ''
  ▼
editor draft (model already '') ──harness switch──▶ ✗ (W3) clears again
  │  ✗ (W2) save refused while fleet does not serve muse
  ▼
persisted '' — the wipe the task reports
```

# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.



# Inspirations
My principles here are inspired by:

- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
- Life isn’t binary (book)
- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)


# Examples

## Intent Driven descriptions

### Bad Example

```js

const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {

    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}

    users.push(user)
  
}

const list = []

userFactory("Frank",32,list)


```

## Good example

```js

/**
* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
*/
const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
  
  return ageNextYear
}

const userObjectsList = []

const usersName = "Frank"
const usersAge = 32

const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})

userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})


```

# Values

## User understandable over technical language

I feel like code should always be understandable by users as they are the ones who dictate process. So the goal of code should make it the most understandable with zero context as possible

### Principles

- Long variables names where needed to be descriptive
- Avoid using technical language such as “factory” or “barrel”
- Stick to a common language profile, (tasks always being tasks, stages always being stages etc)
- File structure should reflect the call stack
- Use of JSDocs to explain variables in pure english
- Include why things are done not just what is done
- Use a labelled data inport pattern (IE  `({varA , varB}) => {}`)
- NEVER MENTION DESIGN PATTERNS
- Use @example tags in js doc to easily explain functionality
  
  

## Functional over Object oreintated

Although pure functional code can tend to insanity it is always important to note co-mingle state and functionality. Where possible state should leave in clearly defined places, and functions should show a clear line in how we move from one state to another. Traditional object oriented design mainly serves to gatekeep devs(or for game dev).

### Principles

- Try and avoid using classes where possible
- Currying can be used to create sudo classes, avoid that
- Functions should follow black box mentality, clear input delivers the same output with no side affects
- Treat variables as immutable unless they are clearly defined states.
- Functions should always be named with a verb in, as they are doing something
- Give the miniumn data to each function as possible. Pick off fields before invocation.
- Each function should only work to achieve its task, with a single responsibility


## Co-location over abstraction

Although abstraction is an essential part of coding it should always only be done by business level intent, not just on functionality. Ideally if you pick a random file in the codebase you should only need to look at the one folder above it and one folder under it to get all the context on its functionality.

### Principles
- Unit tests should always be placed next to the relevant file
- Generally functions called in a higher function should be placed in a folder of that functions name. IE if `funA.js` calls `funB.js` it should be `./funA/funB.js`
- Generic/helper functions should only be made if they are repeatedly doing the same thing.
- Helpers should be treated like react state and exist at the lowest level folder that is common in the hierarchy of the folders
- If abstracting it would take up more lines/characters than just embedding that line directly on a per file basis avoid doing it. IE don’t abstract a single line just because its repeated unless it has some complex logic like a regex.
- Don’t fear repetition of code
- Make sure the code is easily searchable for any given task. If I said modify the task history box in the ui it should  be easy and logical to figure out where that is.
- Use folders as a tool for organising

## Tested over trusted 

Functionality should not assumed to exist until it is tested and evidenced. “it should work” isn’t always reliable and we want to make sure there are no regressions. 

### Principles
- Try and at least plan what tests you are going to make before you  code a function
- Don’t assume typing is correct until proven, or allow it to fail safe
- Failures should clear transparent and observable, every function doesnt need to intensly check it just needs to report failures accurately
- Tests must be consistent
- Integration test must reflect how a user could want to use the app
- Use the lowest possible level of tests( Ie Unit over api over e2e) for the fastest test cycle


## Fast iteration over long planning

Sometimes you just can’t know what will happen without using it and that is essential. Spending too long planning can cause ideas to get confused or get you trapped in a loop where you just make plans worse.  Having simple clear checkpoints is great.

### Principles
- When planning, factor in points to check certain things and how the plan can be adapted when needed
- Try and create safe ways to test functionality, ie not in prod, when possible as this will allow you to confirm things work.
- Focus on one small change at a time, get tests passing then work on the next element.
- Always design code with the intent it will be changed/replaced soon
- Minimise friction in development even if it is small
- Make change easy, then make the change. Even if making change easy is hard.



# Inspirations
My principles here are inspired by:

- Extreme programming Explained by Kent Beck (book)
- Life isn’t binary (book)
- Intent driven design by David whitney (Talk)


# Examples

## Intent Driven descriptions

### Bad Example

```js

const userInOneYearFactory = (name, age, users) => {

    const user = {name: name , age: age + 1}

    users.push(user)
  
}

const list = []

userFactory("Frank",32,list)


```

## Good example

```js

/**
* MARK: calculateAgeNextYear
* @description calculates the age someone will be next year
* @example const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: 3})  
console.log(usersAgeNextYear) // 4
*/
const calculateAgeNextYear = ({ageNow}) => {
  const ageNextYear = ageNow + 1
  
  return ageNextYear
}

const userObjectsList = []

const usersName = "Frank"
const usersAge = 32

const usersAgeNextYear = calculateAgeNextYear({ageNow: usersAge})

userObjectsList.push({name: usersName, age: usersAge})


```

All 341 frontend test files pass (4645 tests). Fixed the flaky focus assertion in `AccessibilityReportDialog`:

      model appears automatically on the next scan; the pin is never
      dropped, so a broken scan cannot hide it). KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_
      DISCOVERY_WINS=1 keeps discovery-replaces-pin as the explicit opt-in.
      Heartbeats label the new state facts.modelSource: "pinned+discovered"
      (accepted by normalizeCapabilities; Settings shows "pinned on Runner +
      auto-detected").

      --no-session-log` with the standard handshake (capabilities: {}),
      matching the backend MSP probe (buildMuseServeSpawnPlan /
      buildMuseMspHandshake), so runner and backend read the same host the
      same way.
    - Re-detect (requestModelRediscovery) now scans pinned runners too.

/***
 * MARK: fleet model options barrel
 * @description Turns fleet catalogue availability (`fleetCountsById`: exact
 *   advertised model ids) into picker options for harnesses the backend
 *   catalogue leaves empty. The backend host can only list models ITS
 *   credentials unlock; the fleet serves more (e.g. a runner's
 *   auto-discovered `muse` menu). Options carry the EXACT advertised id as
 *   their key — dispatch matches requirements against advertised ids
 *   verbatim, so an exact id is a guaranteed matchable selection.
 *
 *   Attribution is strict for harness-scoped ids (`h::p::m` only ever
 *   appears under `h`, so a `pi`-grammar id can never be picked for
 *   `muse`); legacy `provider::id` and bare ids name no harness and appear
 *   under every section the fleet serves them on. Ids already present by
 *   value are never duplicated. Unknown or malformed ids are skipped.
 *
 *   Thin re-export barrel over the one-function-per-file modules in
 *   `./fleetModelOptions/` — keep this entry point so existing callers
 *   (model pickers) need no import changes.
 * @example import { withFleetModels, effectiveModelSelection } from './fleetModelOptions';
 ***/
export { fleetModelsForHarness } from './fleetModelOptions/fleetModelsForHarness.js';
export { fleetServesHarness } from './fleetModelOptions/fleetServesHarness.js';
export { withFleetModels } from './fleetModelOptions/withFleetModels.js';
export { effectiveModelSelection } from './fleetModelOptions/effectiveModelSelection.js';

## Goal

Runners reliably autodetect the models their harnesses can serve (muse first,
then every other leg that shares the bug); those ids are normalized to the
KainBain canonical key grammar, saved into one central model catalogue; and
the UI selects exclusively from that central list — including brand-new

ever silently wiping alias targets.

the UI selects exclusively from that central list — including brand-new
models (e.g. the latest Muse release) and fleet-only harnesses — without
ever silently wiping alias targets.

## Success criteria

1. A new model released in a harness appears as a selectable UI option through
   the normal detection path (no hand-editing of pins or allowlists).
2. One documented central catalogue is the single source the pickers read;
   each option carries its harness attribution and availability.
3. Changing harness availability (offline runner, empty scan, malformed id)
   degrades honestly (marked unavailable / explained warning), never silently.
4. Alias targets are never silently wiped or retargeted by detection changes;
   a missing saved choice keeps the last working value with a warning.
5. `npm run test:unit` and `npm run lint` pass; new behaviour is pinned by
   committed tests.

## Current architecture (verified evidence)

- Runner detection: `runner/daemon.js` (`detectAvailableHarnesses`,
  `refreshDiscoveredModels`, `factsFor`, `SUPPORTED_RUNNER_COMMANDS`),
  per-harness legs in `runner/harnessModelDiscovery.js` reusing each
  backend harness's `listModels()`; muse leg probes `muse serve` stdio
  `model/list` (`runner/modelDiscovery.js` `discoverClaudeModels`).
  Advertisement is pin-wins by default (`resolveAdvertisedModels`),
  discovery-wins opt-in (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MODEL_DISCOVERY_WINS=1`),
  12 h cadence (`MODEL_DISCOVERY_INTERVAL_MS_DEFAULT`), keep-old-slice on
  failure; heartbeat carries `facts.models` + `facts.discoveryStatus`.
- Backend serves TWO catalogues: engine catalogue
  (`aggregateModelCatalog` in `api/models.js`, local harnesses only,
  TTL-cached, curated `FALLBACK_MODELS`) at `GET /compute/models`; fleet
  catalogue (`buildFleetModelCatalog` in
  `api/flow/dispatch/fleetModelCatalog.js`, live-derived from runner
  registrations, never persisted) at `GET /runners/models/catalogue`
  (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`).
- Frontend: `useModelCatalog` reads `/compute/models` (single fetch point);
  `useFleetModelCatalog` reads fleet counts; `ModelSelector` merges fleet
  ids into backend harness sections via `withFleetModels` /
  `fleetModelsForHarness` (`frontend/src/services/fleetModelOptions/`).
  Sections come from the backend `harnesses[]` view — there is no section
  for a harness the backend host itself does not know.
- Grammar: canonical `harness::provider::id(::reasoning)` in
  `shared/modelKeys.js` (single implementation shared backend/frontend).
  The brief's `harness::model::effort` is read as: canonical key + effort
  (tiers/reasoning) carried as catalogue attributes — see Open questions.
- Aliases: `shared/modelAliases.js`; `normalizeModelAliases` drops invalid
  records on write; `ModelAliasesSection.jsx` clears the model on harness
  change (`onTargetChange({ harness: next, model: '' })`); unknown-model is
  currently soft (badge + save succeeds); ADR 0005 owns dispatch combination
  rules.

## Survey mapping (SURVEY.md answers are empty — defaults proposed)

| # | Question | Proposed default (reversible) |
|---|----------|-------------------------------|
| q1 | Scope: muse-only vs all harnesses | Muse first, others only if the same bug affects them |
| q2 | New-model latency | Automatic on next detection/heartbeat; manual Refresh stays as escape hatch |
| q3 | Central list shape | One combined list, each entry labelled with source harness |
| q4 | Offline/broken/empty ids | Keep showing, marked unavailable, with reason |
| q5 | Saved alias choice goes missing | Keep last working choice + warning (never silent wipe) |
| q6 | New model moves aliases? | No — aliases stay; new model is an extra option |

These defaults are assumed unless the task owner answers the survey; each is
flagged at its implementation step so an answer can flip it cheaply.

## Approach — make change easy, then make the change

Research and the two structural enablers come first (Phases 0–1): prove the
exact break in each symptom chain with a failing test before touching
behaviour, and build the seams (fixtures, contract tests, provenance logging)
